title: Can Bamboo Floors Be Refinished? What Most Sammamish Homeowners Get Wrong
meta: Most bamboo floors can be refinished, but strand-woven, engineered and carbonized bamboo behave differently. Wills Flooring explains what works in Sammamish.
keywords: can bamboo floors be refinished, refinish bamboo flooring, sand strand woven bamboo, bamboo floor refinishing cost, bamboo floors Sammamish

blocks.lead: Yes, most solid bamboo floors can be sanded and refinished, at the same $3.99 per sq ft we charge for oak, but the answer changes with the type: strand-woven bamboo sands slowly and hates stain, thin engineered bamboo often cannot be sanded at all, and carbonized bamboo dents easily.
blocks.detail: Bamboo went into thousands of Sammamish homes between 2005 and 2015 as the green alternative to oak. Those floors are now 10 to 20 years old and showing wear. Whether yours can be saved depends on what kind it is, and most owners do not know.

blocks.html: The phone call usually goes like this: a Klahanie or Trossachs homeowner has a bamboo floor from the original build or a 2010 remodel, the finish is scratched gray in front of the sliding door, and two other companies told them bamboo cannot be refinished. That is wrong for most bamboo, but it is also not as simple as sanding oak. Here is what we check before we quote, and what most Sammamish homeowners get wrong about their own floor.

blocks.text: First, figure out which bamboo you have

items.title: Horizontal or vertical solid bamboo
items.text: The classic look with visible nodes (horizontal) or a thin striped look (vertical). Solid strips laminated together, about 5/8 in thick. Sands like a soft hardwood. This is most of the pre-2010 bamboo in Sammamish and the easiest to refinish.

items.title: Strand-woven solid bamboo
items.text: Shredded fibers pressed with resin into a very dense plank, harder than hickory. It refinishes, but the resin clogs sandpaper and the floor takes more passes and more abrasive. We price it the same, but expect an extra day.

items.title: Engineered bamboo
items.text: A bamboo veneer over plywood. Veneers under 2 mm cannot take a full sanding. Some strand-woven engineered products have a 3 mm face and can be sanded once. We measure at a heat register or a threshold before promising anything.

items.title: Carbonized bamboo
items.text: The amber-brown bamboo. The color comes from heat treatment that runs through the whole plank, so it survives sanding, but the same treatment makes it about 30 percent softer. Dog nails and chair legs show fast.

blocks.note: Not sure? A photo of an exposed edge at a register, or the leftover box in the garage, tells us in seconds.

items.html: "Bamboo is a grass, so it cannot be sanded." It is a grass, and it sands fine. What matters is thickness and construction, not botany.

"We will stain it darker to hide the wear." Bamboo has almost no grain to hold stain. Horizontal and vertical bamboo go blotchy, and strand-woven barely accepts stain at all. We steer nearly every bamboo job to a natural finish at $3.99 rather than the $6.50 stain rate.

"It was sold as harder than oak, so it should not be scratched." Only strand-woven is harder than oak. Horizontal and vertical bamboo sit near soft maple, and carbonized bamboo is softer than fir. Big Sammamish dogs on a plateau main floor will scratch it. The finish, not the bamboo, is what protects it.

"The factory finish is the same as a refinish." Most bamboo shipped with a thick aluminum-oxide coating. That is why a light buff and recoat often fails: nothing sticks to it unless it is abraded properly. A recoat at $1.99 works only if we can get real adhesion, and we test a spot first.

"Cupping means the floor is ruined." Bamboo moves with humidity more than oak. Slight cupping in a Beaver Lake home with a damp crawlspace often flattens after the moisture source is fixed, and then it sands flat. Sanding cupped bamboo before fixing the moisture just makes it crown later.

blocks.note: Bamboo is priced at the same rates as hardwood. Strand-woven takes longer but does not cost more per square foot. Choose the natural option; we will explain on site if stain is realistic for your floor.

blocks.text: How a bamboo refinish actually goes

items.text: Identify the type, measure the thickness at a register, check for cupping and test whether the old aluminum-oxide finish can be abraded for a recoat.
items.note: Free in-home visit, firm written price on the spot

items.text: Cut through the factory finish. On strand-woven this is the slow part: coarser grit, more paper changes, and a vacuum-connected sander so the resin dust stays out of the house.
items.note: Dust containment with plastic sealing and an air scrubber is +$250

items.text: Fine sanding, then a water-based sealer and the first coat of Bona finish. Water-based keeps bamboo pale instead of pushing it yellow the way oil-based finishes do.
Two more coats. Socks after 24 hours, furniture after 72, rugs after two weeks. Strand-woven adds about a day to the sanding stage.

a.title: Worth it when
items: Solid bamboo at least 3/32 in above the tongue, or an engineered face of 3 mm or more
Wear is scratches, gray traffic lanes and dull finish, not deep gouges
The floor is flat, or the moisture source that cupped it has been fixed
You are happy with a natural bamboo color rather than a dark stain

b.title: Skip refinishing when
items: Engineered bamboo with a veneer under 2 mm
Planks are delaminating, splintering at the edges or lifting at the ends
Carbonized bamboo in a home with large dogs, since it will dent again within a year
You want a dark or gray floor; bamboo will not get you there evenly

blocks.title: One Sammamish-specific warning:
blocks.text: Plateau homes from the 2000s often have bamboo floating over a crawlspace with marginal ventilation. If the boards cup every winter and flatten every summer, refinishing now will not hold. Fix the crawlspace vapor barrier first, let the floor settle for a season, then sand. We will tell you this at the estimate even though it delays the job.
Checklist before you book a bamboo refinish

items.html: Find out the type. Original paperwork, a leftover box, or a photo of a cut edge. It changes the schedule and whether stain is even an option.
Ask the contractor to measure the thickness. Anyone who quotes bamboo refinishing without checking at a register is guessing.
Fix moisture first. Crawlspace vapor barrier, a leaking fridge line, a sliding door that weeps. Sanding does not fix any of these.
Insist on water-based finish. Three coats of Bona water-based finish keep bamboo its natural blonde and cure hard enough for a busy Sammamish household. Oil-based will amber within a year.

Plan a recoat every 5 to 7 years. Once the aluminum-oxide layer is gone, a $1.99 per sq ft screen and recoat keeps the floor from ever needing a full sand again. See refinish or recoat for how to tell which you need.

Check the warranty and certification. Wills Flooring backs bamboo refinishing with the same 1-year workmanship warranty as hardwood, and our crews are Bona Certified Craftsmen. Learn more on our refinishing service page.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish bamboo floors in Sammamish?
faq.a: The same as hardwood at Wills Flooring: $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish and $1.99 for a screen and recoat, with a 500 sq ft minimum. A 1,200 sq ft main floor is $4,788 for a full refinish. Strand-woven bamboo takes longer but is not priced higher.

Yes. It is very hard and the resin loads up sandpaper quickly, so it takes coarser grits, more paper and roughly an extra day compared with oak. The result is excellent because the surface is so dense. Expect a natural finish; strand-woven takes stain poorly.

faq.q: Can bamboo floors be stained a different color?
faq.a: Rarely with good results. Bamboo has no real grain to hold pigment, so horizontal and vertical bamboo go blotchy and strand-woven barely changes. We usually recommend a clear water-based finish. If you want a dark or gray floor, replacing with hardwood or vinyl plank is the honest answer.

faq.q: How many times can bamboo be refinished?
faq.a: Solid bamboo at 5/8 in thick can usually take two to three full sandings over its life, similar to a 3/4 in oak floor. Engineered bamboo with a 3 mm face can take one careful sanding. Anything thinner should be recoated only, or replaced.

faq.q: Is bamboo a good floor for a Sammamish family with dogs?
faq.a: Strand-woven, yes. Horizontal, vertical and especially carbonized bamboo dent under big dogs and dining chairs. If you already have a soft bamboo floor, a refinish with a hard water-based finish and a satin sheen hides wear best, but it will not make the bamboo harder.
